title: Yankees bullpen takes another hit as reliever Fernando Cruz heads to injured list
content:
NEW YORK — The New York Yankees’ taxed bullpen took another blow Wednesday when the team put right-hander Fernando Cruz — typically one of its best late-inning options — on the injured list with elbow discomfort.

The injury may explain Cruz’s poor performance of late.

Cruz gave up a two-run home run in a 9-7 loss to the Houston Astros on Tuesday night at Yankee Stadium. The Athletic’s Chris Kirschner saw Cruz leave the clubhouse late Tuesday night accompanied by a Yankees trainer.

Cruz has been awful since the All-Star break, posting a 5.52 ERA over 17 games (14 2/3 innings).

The Yankees also made a bevy of other moves.

They signed righty Michael Fulmer to a big-league deal and added him to the active roster to replace Cruz. Fulmer, 33, has made just three MLB appearances this season, all of them with the Los Angeles Angels. Fulmer elected free agency Tuesday after the Angels designated him for assignment Sunday. He had a 2.98 ERA in 37 appearances at Triple A with the San Francisco Giants. He won the AL Rookie of the Year in 2016 and was an All-Star in 2017 as a starting pitcher, but has been primarily a reliever since 2021. The Yankees also called up righty prospect Elmer Rodríguez, who will start Wednesday night against the Astros.

Right-handed reliever Bradley Hanner was demoted to Triple A, and another righty reliever, Kervin Castro, was moved to the 60-day IL with elbow neuritis.

Cruz didn’t mention elbow pain when he spoke to reporters after Tuesday’s loss.

“There’s ups and downs like every player has,” Cruz said of his recent struggles. “It’s been a lot of stuff regarding that, that we’re on top of. Just gotta be better. It’s gonna come. My splitter hasn’t been as effective. A little bit of a mechanical change. We’re playing (against) Major League Baseball players, and they’re really good at it. I think they made the change. Now we have to adjust.”

The Yankees didn’t trade for a reliever at the Aug. 3 deadline, and all they have done is take hits. They also have righty Angel Chivilli (elbow discomfort) on the injured list.

They have received stellar work from the rest of their high-leverage relievers, a group that includes lefty Brent Headrick and righties Paul Blackburn and David Bednar, the closer. But the trio has been used heavily in recent weeks as the Yankees’ offense has sputtered and been unable to produce big leads.
